parties:
Nung Shu Kumur Deb
Vs.
1. General Certificate Officer and others
2. Moklesur Rahman
full_judgment:
Md. Abdus Salam, J: This appeal has been preferred by the plaintiff against the impugned order dated 18.2.1996 passed by Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 87 of 1995 directing the plaintiff-appellant to furnish Bank Guarantee of Tk. 43 lacs and passing conditional injunction order, mainly on the grounds, that the impugned judgment and order of furnishing Bank Guarantee is bad in law and that in such a case there cannot be any order of Bank Guarantee since it is the bid money or part thereof which the bidder is to pay as per tender floated by the bank through Certificate Officer, hence the Order of furnishing Bark Guarantee is not sustainable in law; that the defendants in their written objection did not raise any such point and did not pray for such Bank Guarantee and the trial Court while granting the relief of temporary injunction cannot impose a condition and the condition of furnishing Bank Guarantee has made the order of injunction in fructuous and that the plaintiff appellant has been fighting to purchase the garden and is ready with the highest offer to fulfill all the conditions of the tender; hence the observation of the trial Court that there is no certainty that the plaintiff will purchase the garden at Tk. 43 laces and this observation is unjustified and as such the impugned order of furnishing Bank Guarantee is illegal. 

 2. The plaintiff-appellant filed the suit for declaration and thereafter filed an application under Order 39, Rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure for temporary injunction retraining defendant Nos. 1-4 from transferring the M/s Halda Valley Tea Garden and its movable and immovable property by auction sale in favour of defendant No. 5 or any other person till disposal of the suit. The M/s. Halda Valley Tea Garden and its share-holders took loan from defendant No. 2, Bangladesh Krishi Bank for development of their Tea Garden but the share holders of the Tea Garden could not pay the Bank dues, hence defendant Nos. 3 and 4 as officers of defendant No. 2 Krishi Bank brought Certificate Case No. 812(G)/1990-91 in the office of defendant No. 1 Certificate Officer and after issuing notice in the daily news papers, 6.5.91 was fixed for holding auction sale; the plaintiff-appellants participated in the auction purchase and expressed his willingness to purchase the Garden at Tk. 43 lacs; Advocate Amir Faisal, Md. Abdullah and Nasiruddin Bahadur also participated in the bid and offered to purchase the Garden at Tk. 42 lacs, 41 lacs and 38 lacs respectively. It is alleged that the plaintiff appellant was the highest bidder, in spite of that defendant No. 1 on the advice of defendant No. 2-4 did not sell the Tea Garden in favour of the plaintiff and floated another auction notice in the daily Ittefaq dated 22.3.93 but there was no response from any bidder to purchase the Tea Garden. Thereafter defendant No. 4 issued a letter dated 3.2.94 to the bidders for negotiation but nobody else offered any higher bid money than the bid money of plaintiff-appellant; inspite of that defendant Nos. 2-4 in the hope of illegal gain took initiative to sell the Tea Garden to another person only at a price of Tk. 20 lacs, the defendant appellant submitted an objection against this move but defendant No. 2 - 4 took final steps for selling the Tea Garden in favour of defendant No. 5 only at a price of Tk. 25 lacs. Under this circumstance the plaintiff-appellant filed the suit and prayed for temporary injunction. 

 3. The Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong heard the application for temporary injunction and the written objection and passed the impugned order No. 8 dated 18.2.96 granting temporary injunction with a precondition that the plaintiff-appellant is to ensure as a real purchaser of the Tea Garden by furnishing a Bank Guarantee of Tk. 43 lacs within two months, in default the application for temporary injunction shall stand dismissed. Being aggrieved by this impugned order the plaintiff appellant filed this miscellaneous appeal. 

 4. Mr. M.A. Jalil, the learned Advocate for plaintiff appellant argued supporting all the grounds of the memorandum of appeal and submits that the trial Court committed error of law by imposing a condition of finishing Bank Guarantee in the order of temporary injunction and this type of conditional injunction is illegal and infructuous, hence the condition of furnishing bank guarantee is to be deleted and the defendant respondent should be restrained from transferring the suit. Tea Garden to any body else including defendant No. 5 till disposal of the suit. 

 5. Mr. Israil Hossain, learned Advocate, for respondent No. 3, General Manager of Bangladesh Krishi Bank filed affidavit-in opposition and argued supporting the grounds stated therein and submits that the declaratory suit filed by the appellant is not maintainable in law and it is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that Bangladesh Krishi Bank filed the Certificate Case under section 10(A) of Public Demand Recovery Act and that on the auction sale date on 20.12.1992 the appellant was the highest bidder at Tk. 43 lacs but he did not deposit 25% of the bid money under Rule 68 of Schedule No. 2 of Pubalic Demands Recovery Act and inspite of subsequent correspondences with him the plaintiff appellant expressed his inability to deposit the bid money; on a subsequent sale date fixed under Rule 50, respondent No. 5 was the highest bidder at Tk. 25 lacs and he also agreed to pay land improvement tax of Tk. 23 lacs, hence the bid money stood at Tk. 48 lacs and his bid was accepted. The plaintiff appellant being a defaulter his bid was not accepted and as such he has no locus-standi to challenge the order of Certificate Court. The learned Counsel for respondent No. 3 further submits that Bangladesh Krishi Bank is governed by the special provisions of section 10 (A) of the Public Demand Recovery Act and Article 21 of Bangladesh Krishi Bank's Order 1973 which are good laws as held by Appellate Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court in a case reported in 50 D.L.R. (AD) page 194 and that the amount mentioned in the Certificate Case is a conclusive proof that it is due to the Bank and Certificate Officer is bound to execute it without any right to entertain any objection against the bid from anybody including the plaintiff-appellant; hence it is finally submitted that the plaintiff-appellant has got no prima-facie case, the original suit is not prima-facie maintainable and that this appeal has got no merit. 

 7. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, learned Deputy Attorney General assisted by Mr. Zainul Abedin, learned A.A.G. And Mr. Toufique Hossain, A.A.G. argued supporting the case of the respondents and submits that the suit is not maintainable and the plaintiff appellant has no locus-standi to challenge the order of the General Certificate Officer and that the impugned order passed by the Subordinate judge, Chittagong is liable to be set aside and this appeal has got no merit. 

 11. Admittedly the Plaintiff appellant did not deposit the mandatory 25% of his purchase money and in the eye of law he is a defaulter having no right to purchase the suit Tea Garden, under this circumstances the defendant respondents had to process the subsequent sale of the suit Tea Garden, hence in our view the suit filed by the plaintiff-appellant is prima facie not maintainable and the trial Court passed the impugned order of temporary injunction illegally, no question of furnishing Bank Guarantee arises at all. Since the suit is prima-facie not maintainable in law for the aforesaid reasons this appeal has got no merit.
